text:
olivia: Hey team, a customer reported a sudden billing bump this morning. SDK estimator shows ~1,240 tokens but invoice shows ~2,010 tokens for the same session. They use streaming, single-turn chat, no tool calls.

sara: Ugh, can you paste the request + headers (no secrets)?

olivia: Pasted minimal repro below. Note: SDK local estimate = 1,240, API/console shows 1,240 tokens on the request page, invoice charged 2,010. Customer says this started after a session reconnect pattern.

olivia: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the document."}],"stream":true,"session_id":"sess-7f8a"}'
```

ashley: I can repro locally with a quick script that simulates a streaming reconnect + finalization. It looks like the server is appending a hidden terminal marker and a short metadata blob when the session is closed by the backend, which our client estimator doesn’t account for.

ashley: Quick log extract from runtime:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:33Z] session sess-7f8a: applied_terminal_marker {"eos":"\u0002","meta_len":42} -> added 42 bytes -> ~65 tokens
```

mike: Can you quantify the gap? The invoice difference ~770 tokens — is that all from the terminal marker?

ashley: Not entirely. Two contributors: (1) terminal/meta blob (~40-100 tokens depending on encoding) and (2) a small padding snippet added on reconnect to preserve KV alignment (~600 tokens in this workload because model prompted with long prefix + KV re-serialization).

olivia: Example numbers from the customer's payload:
- client SDK estimate: 1,240 tokens
- API response token count (in JSON returned): 1,240 tokens
- invoice line units: 2,010 tokens
- delta: 770 tokens (invoice > client)

tom: Interesting that API response count matches SDK. That implies metering is counting post-processing additions that are not surfaced in the completion response body. ai_meter_bot should have an audit log. @ai_meter_bot can you pull metering extras for sess-7f8a between timestamps 2026-03-15T09:12 and 09:15?

ai_meter_bot: Audit dump for sess-7f8a (redacted): [server_prefill: 62 tokens], [terminal_blob: 48 tokens], [kv_reserialize: 660 tokens] -> total extras = 770 tokens.

sara: Thanks. So the root cause is server-side additions (prefill/terminal/kv) not included in the returned token count or the SDK estimator. Customer-facing mitigation: update SDK estimator to include an optional "server_overhead" heuristic, and doc the case when streaming reconnects occur.

mike: Billing note: these extras are billable per our current metering policy (they are part of the final serialized request units). We should provide customers an invoice breakdown to make this transparent.

olivia: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate. Proposed steps I shared with them:
1) open a streaming session with session_id=any
2) send a single-user turn with a large prompt prefix (we used ~1,800 tokens)
3) deliberately trigger a reconnect (close stream mid-response and reattach)
4) check SDK estimator vs invoice after 24h

ashley: Engineering action items:
- add instrumentation to show server_injected_token_types in /v1/usage/detail for sessions (short-term).
- make the runtime avoid adding large KV reserialization on reconnect for small customers (medium-term).

tom: Devex: add FAQ entry and an SDK flag `include_server_overhead:true` for local estimation so customers can opt into conservative estimates.

olivia: I'll loop the customer back with the repro + temporary workaround (patch SDK to add +770 tokens for their workload) and offer to raise a billing credit if they need immediate relief.

sara: Thanks, team. Marking as support-escalation resolved once customer confirms or accepts credit. :thumbsup:
